summaries.evidence: Existing pinned primary-source review and official code bindings read locally.
summaries.summary: HUG separates object-relative fingertip quality and execution, uses an approximate MANO physics hand, and uses embodiment-specific robot retargeting. Those results motivate separate geometry and outcome evidence; they supply no universal native-to-Shadow tolerance.

Reports contact-link object-relative displacement, bone alignment and penetration separately from downstream tracking. Contact links use ContactPose annotations that this project lacks. Its experiment excludes three deeply concave objects including a mug; our metrics must be labeled geometric proxies, and neither its results nor thresholds transfer as Shadow acceptance limits.

Optimizes human/robot hand keypoint vectors under joint limits with a hand-size scale and temporal regularization. That hand-only objective is a useful baseline structure; passing its optimization does not establish object-relative fidelity or a universal practical accuracy margin.
